newsitem.title: USA: Apple shares crushed in early trading.
newsitem.headline: Apple shares crushed in early trading.

text.p: The stock of Apple Computer Inc. sold off sharply ahead of Monday's market opening after it announced Friday that weak demand for its Performa line of personal computers will lead to an operating loss of $100 million to $150 million in its latest quarter.
Apple shares tumbled $4 to $17.75 on the Instinet system. They reversed course slightly, but remained lower in the $18 to $18.25 range after closing Friday at $21.75 on Nasdaq.
Prudential Securities lowered its recommendation on Apple to hold from buy, according to a source at the brokerage house.

Apple on Friday blamed a shortage of PowerBook laptops and slow sales of its Performa line -- which is geared toward home users -- for the expected shortfall in its first quarter, which ended last month. Consumer sales traditionally account for 40 percent of Apple's Christmas quarter.
Revenue for the quarter ended Dec. 27 will be about 10 percent less than the $2.3 billion reported in the September quarter, Apple said.
Apple Chairman Gilbert Amelio was expected to outline his company's turnaround strategy on Tuesday to thousands of Macintosh customers and programmers at the Macworld trade show.

Amelio said Friday the company would have to reduce its expenses by about $1 billion to $8 billion annually to return to profit. That could include another round of firings after the company laid off about 1,300 people last year.
